report.source_text: On hospital day one, the patient's left lower extremity symptoms persisted, prompting a second left lower extremity venogram and cavogram. This revealed persistent thrombus within the left superficial, common femoral, external iliac, and common iliac veins, although the popliteal and distal superficial femoral artery remained patent. Notably, there was interval improvement in clot burden with no significant stenosis at the level of the proximal common iliac vein. However, a severe stenosis of 75% was identified at the left common femoral and iliac veins.

report.source_text: The IR team, in collaboration with the medical team, reached a consensus to proceed with mechanical thrombectomy, which was performed at the left superficial femoral, common femoral, and iliac veins using a 10 mm balloon. Despite initial balloon dilation of the left common femoral vein stenosis, refractory stenosis persisted, with significant residual stenosis of more than 50% (Figure 2). Consequently, a 10 mm drug-eluting balloon was employed, resulting in interval improvement in flow and caliber, with a residual stenosis of 30%. Further, a 12 mm balloon was used to dilate the left iliac vein stenosis; however, stenosis refractory to previous dilations persisted, with a residual stenosis of more than 50%. To address this, a 12 x 60 mm Life Star self-expanding stent was deployed within the left iliac vein, centered on the area of critical stenosis (Figure 3). Subsequent balloon dilation with a 12 mm balloon demonstrated interval improvement in flow and caliber, with no significant residual thrombus.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old Hispanic gentleman presented with left lower extremity swelling and pain. Initial Doppler ultrasonography revealed occlusive DVT in the left calf, extending to the left femoral vein, and chronic DVT in the right popliteal veins. An initial venogram was performed, which the final diagnosis states confirmed MTS. A second venogram on hospital day one further revealed persistent thrombus and severe stenosis (75%) at the left common femoral and iliac veins. The patient underwent mechanical thrombectomy, balloon dilation, and stenting of the left iliac vein.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with left lower extremity swelling and pain.
Initial Doppler ultrasonography showed occlusive DVT in the left calf, extending to the left femoral vein, and involvement of superficial small saphenous and great saphenous veins.
Chronic occlusive DVT was identified in the right popliteal veins.
A venogram was obtained which confirmed the diagnosis of MTS, with patent distal IVC and the catheter tip in the IVC.

A second left lower extremity venogram and cavogram on hospital day one revealed persistent thrombus within the left superficial, common femoral, external iliac, and common iliac veins, and a severe stenosis of 75% at the left common femoral and iliac veins.
Intervention included mechanical thrombectomy, balloon dilation, and deployment of a self-expanding stent within the left iliac vein to address refractory stenosis.
